body:
PR-2808 at 61888258f6: CHANGES REQUESTED. Every earlier ruling is verified; this is ONE new MAJOR plus small items. Keep the round narrow. Full text: .aida/review-verdicts/PR-2808.json

* MAJOR — false zero-reader refusal under PID-namespaced sandboxes. mailbox_resolver.rs:71-77 builds live_ids via agent_registry::registry_entry_is_live -> aida_core::liveness::process_identity_is_alive -> pid_is_alive (liveness.rs:1043-1050, libc::kill(pid,0)). Inside Claude Code's bubblewrap sandbox the caller has its own PID namespace ($$=2, /proc lists 5 pids), so every registry pid returns ESRCH. Evidence at this head's environment: 'aida agent ls' (same registry_entry_is_live) prints 'No active agents found.' while .aida/agents/claude-862809.toml (role=advisor, last_active 05:34Z) and claude-1426585.toml (role=reviewer, last_active 05:52Z = this review session) are live. Under this PR, mailbox_cmd.rs Send and punt_done.rs resolve_comment_mentions run in that sandboxed CLI process, so 'aida mailbox send --to advisor' from any sandboxed agent bails 'advisor has 0 live readers' and named-agent sends bail 'no live agent' — the implementer->advisor READY/report channel breaks and the error falsely claims nobody is reading (main only warned). MCP sends are unaffected because the MCP server is unsandboxed. Fix: treat liveness the caller cannot observe (pid outside the caller's PID namespace / probe ESRCH while the caller is namespaced) as unknown rather than dead — e.g. fall back to a fresh last_active_at heartbeat, or warn-and-deliver instead of refuse — and add a unit test with an injected unobservable-liveness probe proving a role send still delivers (or refuses with an accurate message). 

* MINOR — person/role collision now refuses. mailbox_resolver.rs:131-138 counts role+person; a team roster member spelled like a role (e.g. 'Advisor = []', the shape the PR's own historical_catalog_preserves_precedence_while_live_catalog_addresses_win fixture uses at line 444) makes '--to advisor' bail 'ambiguous recipient', whereas main delivered to the stored spelling. Either pin the intended precedence (person or role wins) or keep refusing but cover it with a live-resolver test and a hint naming the two kinds. 

* MINOR — refusal hints are not actionable in PR1. mailbox_resolver.rs:168/202/203 tell the sender to 'name a live agent handle', but handles do not exist until PR2 and the C1 --queue-for-role escape is deferred (ruling 81b4a4f8), so an implementer whose advisor is offline has no documented way to leave mail. The CLI hint should name what works today (a live agent's launch name, a known person inbox, or --broadcast); the MCP text can stay free of the CLI-only 'aida agent ls' hint. 

* COSMETIC — docs/cli/06-roles-sessions.md:251-252 repeats the '<!-- trace:STORY-1843 | ai:codex -->' line twice. 

ADVISOR RULINGS:
MAJOR (false zero-reader refusal in PID-namespaced sandboxes): liveness the sender CANNOT observe must never become a refusal. Record the PID-namespace identity (inode of /proc/self/ns/pid) in the registry entry, or detect that the caller's namespace differs. When a live check is unknowable from the caller's namespace, the entry counts as "unknown", and an unknown-liveness role recipient is DELIVERED to the durable role inbox, not refused. Refuse only on positive evidence that zero readers exist. Test: a registry entry from another PID namespace (inject the namespace id, or simulate kill() ESRCH with a namespace mismatch) gives a delivery, not a refusal.
MINOR person/role collision: a roster PERSON whose name equals a ROLE does not create ambiguity. The role meaning wins for `--to <role>`, and the person stays reachable as person:<name>. Pin with a test using the fixture shape at line 444.
MINOR hints: PR1 hints must name an escape that exists today, e.g. mail the operator (`--to joe` or the person inbox) or `aida comment add <SPEC>`. Mention handles only once PR2 lands.
COSMETIC: drop the duplicate trace line in docs/cli/06-roles-sessions.md.
Push a normal commit, wait for green CI on the new head, then mail READY. Reach a quiet point before any handoff.
